method_note: Static read of viewer.html (17.9k lines) plus the live computed-style inventory Paul supplied (110 button elements, 31 visible signatures, 10 button radii, 20 radii file-wide) — that inventory was taken as given and not re-derived. Say or ask one thing without deciding where it goes (the composer — the only surface she has reached for unprompted, 2026-07-26).
Settle a question only someone standing on the property can settle, without risking being wrong (Mama's Perspective).
Know that what she gave the app was received and mattered (the ack ribbon).

Card expansion is rare (card_expanded fired 4 times in 30 days across 15 sessions), so most surfaces are read at the glance layer and never opened.

findings.observation: There is no button layer in this file — only 110 individually-authored controls. 31 visible signatures and 10 radii (0, 6, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 22, 50%) is not drift; it is the arithmetic of a codebase where every button was styled at the moment it was needed and nothing ever declared what a button IS. Each of the six waves since May correctly fixed the button in front of it (the ✓/× grammar 5/22, the 44px floor 8/01, the four-card shell 7/30) and none of them could fix the class, because the class was never named.
findings.user_impact: For a reader who routes by shape before she reads a word, 31 signatures means the surface teaches nothing. She cannot learn 'a green rectangle sends' or 'a pill answers', because both statements are false somewhere in the app. Every new screen is a first encounter. And for Paul: the next button will be signature #32, because inventing one is currently cheaper than finding the right one.
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen #4 (consistency and standards) + Norman (one signifier, one meaning) + 'Content and function first; form follows — and then form has to be excellent' (intentional · professional · clean · holistic)
findings.recommendation:
Add a token block at the top of the stylesheet and four role classes, then map every existing button onto one role. Tokens (put immediately after the `* { box-sizing }` rule so they precede every use):

:root {
  --r-shell: 18px;   /* .main-card, the outermost containers */
  --r-shelf: 16px;   /* .ref-drawer-toggle, sheets */
  --r-card:  14px;   /* .ic-card, modals, panels */
  --r-block: 12px;   /* .wblock, .dash-cell, in-card panels */
  --r-ctrl:  10px;   /* every COMMITTING button, and every text input */
  --r-chip:   8px;   /* small chrome: src-tags, data cells, icon squares */
  --r-pill:  999px;  /* choice chips — a pill at ANY height, see F3 */
  --r-round:  50%;   /* circular icon buttons */
  --btn-gap:  8px;   /* the only gap inside a control row */
}

Four roles, and the RULE is that a new visual signature is a claim that a fifth role exists — which needs an argument, not a paint job:

.btn-commit  — sends, saves, opens a flow. radius var(--r-ctrl); filled forest gradient (#2f5a3a→#1f4528); Crimson 16px/600 white; min-height 52px (60 in text-lg); fills its row; label centered; NO glyph.
              members: .ui-action-btn.ui-save-btn, .mom-queue-launcher-go, .feedback-send (currently 12px / DM Sans 15px / 44px — bring it in).
.btn-choice  — one option in a set. radius var(--r-pill); Crimson 14px/600; min-height 44px (52 in text-lg); hugs its label; exactly three fills — affirmative filled #3a6a3a + ✓, negative white + 2px #b8a878 + ×, neutral white + 2px #d8cca0 no glyph. THIS IS THE 2026-07-29 RULE, UNCHANGED — it is being named, not altered.
              members: .gg-suggest-btn-yes / -no / -neutral, .gg-followup-chip, .gg-log-btn, .mom-queue-addnote (dashed border = the modifier variant, keep).
.btn-quiet   — chrome: toggles, nav arrows, sync, radar, sound, glyph buttons. radius var(--r-chip) or var(--r-round); no fill or a pale fill; DM Sans 11.5–13px; painted at its natural size with the hit area grown to 44px by the EXISTING ::after mechanism at line 44–58.
              members: .radar-toggle-btn (6→8), .fn-sync-btn (6→8), .mom-queue-nav-arrow (10→8), .bio-sound-btn (50%, unchanged), .ui-glyph-btn, .pmap-ctrl-btn, .feedback-close.
.btn-link    — a control that lives inside a sentence. No box, no radius except a 3px focus ring, inherits the surrounding type, underlined.
              members: .ack-inline-link, .ic-head-link, .mom-queue-general-toggle, .mom-queue-launcher-dismiss, .ui-reset-btn.

Everything else that is currently a button and fits none of these is a TAB (see F7) or a CARD (.dash-cell — a container that happens to be tappable, correctly outside this system). Put the role classes in the markup alongside the existing class names rather than renaming anything: `class="btn-choice gg-suggest-btn-yes"`. The specific class then carries only fill and glyph; geometry lives in the role. That is what makes conforming cheaper than inventing.

findings.observation: The two shapes Paul is reacting to — the r22 pill ('Got it', 'Something's missing', 'Write back') and the r10 rounded rect ('Save & consult the Almanac', 'I've got a minute') — are not arbitrary. They already correlate almost perfectly with a real distinction: the pills are things she picks FROM a set and that stay on the surface; the rects are things she COMMITS and that hand off to a flow. The exception that proves it is `.mom-queue-addnote`, which is a pill (r22) doing a commit-shaped job (full-width, opens a box), and `.feedback-send`, which is a rect at r12 rather than r10.
findings.user_impact: The system she needs is 90% built and undeclared, which is the worst state: it is consistent often enough to teach a rule and inconsistent often enough to break it. A rule broken once is worse than no rule, because she learns it and then it fails her.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Content and function first; form follows' — the Porsche reading: form derived from function reads as inevitable. Here the derivation already happened and was never written down. + Nielsen #6 (recognition over recall)
findings.recommendation: Write the rule as the shape system in F1 and change almost nothing: SHAPE IS THE ROLE. Pill = a choice among options, hugs its label, stays on the surface. Rounded rect (10px) = a commit, fills its row, hands off. Circle / small chip = chrome. Then fix the two outliers: `.feedback-send` 12px→var(--r-ctrl); `.mom-queue-addnote` stays a pill (it IS a choice — the fourth door on a confirm card, per the 7/26 F9 finding that it is the only move she cannot be wrong about) but stops being full-width and joins the row grid (F9). Do NOT reshape `.gg-suggest-btn-*` — they are the ratified components.

findings.observation: `.gg-suggest-btn-yes/-no/-neutral` and `.mom-queue-addnote` use `border-radius: 22px` with `min-height: 44px`. At 44px a 22px radius is exactly a pill. But `body.text-lg` raises the same buttons to `min-height: 52px` (lines 4489, 4610, 5628–5629) and does not touch the radius — so in A+ mode, the mode Mom is most likely using, the app's affirmative control is a rounded rectangle with 4px of flat edge top and bottom, and it now shares its silhouette with `.ui-action-btn` (r10, 60px in A+). The one shape rule the app has stops holding in the one text mode it was written for. `.gg-followup-chip` and `.gg-log-btn` have the same 22px and no text-lg height override, so they stay pills — meaning in A+ the chips and the answer buttons stop matching each other too.
findings.user_impact: This is the 2026-07-29 rule silently not holding. Paul's words were 'a consistent signal of we hear you' — and the signal is fill + glyph + shape. Two of the three survive A+; the third quietly doesn't. It is invisible on a desktop viewport at default text size, which is exactly the blind spot that produced the 16px input floor and the 44px tap floor.
findings.principle_invoked: ONE affirmative grammar everywhere she taps (Paul-stated 2026-07-29) + 'Make every surface read at half-engagement' (the bar is set by the worst-case context, not the best)
findings.recommendation: Replace `border-radius: 22px` with `border-radius: var(--r-pill)` (999px) on `.gg-suggest-btn-yes, .gg-suggest-btn-no`, `.gg-suggest-btn-neutral`, `.mom-queue-addnote`, `.gg-followup-chip`, `.gg-log-btn`, and `.ui-input-row`. 999px is a pill at 44px, at 52px, and at any height a future text mode introduces — the shape becomes size-independent by construction rather than by a number that happens to match today's height. ⚠️ This touches the ratified components, so it needs Paul's nod even though it is repairing his rule rather than changing it. Verification: toggle A+ and confirm all six read as pills at 390px.

findings.observation: Width and alignment are assigned per-button with no rule. Live: 88px / 101px / 167px (hug, in a wrapping flex row), 606px (`.mom-queue-addnote`, `display:block; width:100%`), 606px (`.mom-queue-launcher-go`, `width:100%`), 210px (`.ui-action-btn`, `flex:1; min-width:140px` inside `.ui-action-row { margin-left:auto }` — i.e. right-aligned, and at ≤480px additionally `margin-right: 58px`). So on one card stack the reader meets a hugging pill, a full-bleed pill, a full-bleed rect, and a right-aligned partial-width rect.
findings.user_impact: Width is the loudest signal on a control after fill, and it is currently carrying nothing. She cannot use 'this one goes all the way across' to mean anything, because it means three different things.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Ordering first, then type in service of it' — extended from type to geometry: a visual property that varies without meaning is noise + Nielsen #4
findings.recommendation: One rule, two lines: A `.btn-commit` FILLS its row and centers its label. A `.btn-choice` HUGS its label and sits in an even row grid (F9). Nothing hugs and centers itself in the middle of a row. Two documented exceptions stay and get a comment so nobody 'fixes' them: (1) `.ui-action-row { margin-right: 58px }` at ≤480px is measured clearance for the fixed feedback ribbon (2026-08-01), not sloppy alignment — the button still fills the row it has; (2) `.mom-queue-launcher-dismiss` (90×25) is Paul's ratified small-target exception (2026-08-02) and is a `.btn-link`, not a button. Also drop `min-width: 140px` from `.ui-action-btn` once it fills its row — it is a leftover from the retired two-button Save/Ask split and can only fight the flex basis.

findings.recommendation: The emoji policy, stated once so it holds: A GLYPH ON A BUTTON MUST CARRY THE DECISION, NEVER THE TOPIC. Permitted: the ✓ and × on `.btn-choice` — they encode the answer independent of label legibility, which is why they exist and why they are Paul-stated. Not permitted: a topic emoji on a `.btn-commit`; the topic is the card's job and the card header already does it. Concretely: delete `.mom-queue-launcher-emoji` from the markup and the CSS, and drop the '＋' from '＋ Add a note' (see F16). ⚠️ SEQUENCING COLLISION: this is a chrome change inside the launcher's clean measurement window closing 2026-08-10, and the 7/30 review (F12) said one confound is recoverable and two stacked are not — the shell restyle already spent the one. findings.observation: A filled dark-green pill means two unrelated things in this app. On Mom's surfaces it is `gg-suggest-btn-yes` — 'yes, and it's recorded' — the ratified affirmative. In the Fishing section, `.fish-tab.active` is a filled #1a5a3a pill at r20, meaning 'this species tab is selected.' Separately, the app runs two tab grammars at once: `.fish-tab` (pill, filled-when-active, r20) and `.plant-view-tab` / `.wildlife-tab` (r0, text with an underline-when-active) — same job, switching which slice of a card you are reading.
findings.user_impact: Rule 1 works by making one shape mean one thing everywhere she taps. Spending the filled-green pill on a tab state dilutes the signal the rule depends on, and it does so on a card she can reach. And two tab grammars means the app teaches 'tabs look like this' twice, differently.
findings.principle_invoked: ONE affirmative grammar everywhere she taps (Paul-stated 2026-07-29) — its enforcement half: a grammar only holds if the signal is reserved + Norman (one signifier, one meaning)
findings.recommendation: Make `.fish-tab` adopt the underline grammar the plant and wildlife tabs already use: r0, transparent background, `border-bottom: 2px solid` transparent → #2a6040 when active, `font-weight: 700` when active, keeping its `min-height: 44px` and horizontal scroll. Two gains: the filled-green pill is returned to the affirmative, and the app has ONE tab grammar. Tabs are then formally outside the button system (they select a view; they do not act), which is worth stating in the same comment block as the roles. This is fishing — Paul's own surface, not Mom's — so the cost is low and the signal it frees is on hers.

findings.observation: Paul's 'the action row sits on top of a row where something's missing' is a wrap artifact and it is computable. `.gg-suggest-actions` is `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px` inside `.ic-card`, which gives 336px of content at 390px. The three buttons measure ≈125px ('✓ Looks right'), ≈117px ('× Not quite') and ≈136px ('I haven't looked', the global deferral from a474276) — 394px including gaps. So line 1 takes the two verdicts (250px) and the deferral wraps alone onto line 2, leaving ~200px of empty row to its right. Below it: a hint line, then `.mom-queue-addnote` at full 606px width. Four different widths in four stacked rows.
findings.user_impact: An empty half-row reads as a control that failed to load. For a reader who routes by position and shape, ragged wrap is the single most legible way to say 'something is broken here' without saying anything. It also lands on the card whose entire job is making her feel she cannot get it wrong.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Ordering first, then type in service of it' + Nielsen #8 (aesthetic and minimalist design) + Norman (a gap in a row is a signifier whether or not you meant it to be)

findings.observation: The weather card runs TWO independent rule cascades over the same four inputs. `generateGardenerInsight()` (7233–7381) is a first-match-wins cascade returning one {observation, action}. `generateAlerts()` (8154+) is an all-match cascade returning a list — and its rules fire on the same drivers at neighbouring thresholds: active rain (rate>0.02 vs >0.05), saturated soil (todayTotal>0.75 vs >0.5), heat, freezing, falling pressure. On a wet afternoon the reader gets, within ~200px: 'Worth knowing → It's raining at the gauge · Property gauge: 0.15"/hr — 0.40" today so far', then the glance → 'Rain in progress (0.15"/hr) — 0.40" today so far', then the 📡 hero → '72°F · 88% humidity · light · 0.40" today · 0.15"/hr', then the rainfall panel → Now 0.15"/hr, Today 0.40", by-day Today 0.40". Two numbers, four places, three phrasings.
findings.user_impact: This is the mechanism behind Paul's 'multiple summaries from different sources about the conditions right now.' It is worse than clutter: the two cascades have different thresholds, so they can legitimately DISAGREE — at rate 0.03 the alert says it is raining and the glance does not mention rain at all. On the card whose credibility is 'measured on your property,' a surface that contradicts itself is the costliest failure available, and it is the one that produced her rainfall report on 7/26.
findings.principle_invoked: One engine, one verdict (fernwood.md) — this is its confirming SECOND OCCURRENCE. 7/06 fished out two compute paths for one species phase; 7/14 reconciled the collapsed header with the card body under one generator; the alerts cascade was the third path and was never brought in. + 'A relabel is not a re-rank' (7/26 proposal) — the 7/14 wave named the sources correctly and did not merge the engines.

findings.observation: Paul's root-cause trace is correct and it is broader than the muggy rule. Six of the insight rules bake a measured or forecast NUMBER into the observation string: 7286 (rate + today), 7293 (today), 7300 (temp + dew point), 7316–7318 (today's high + current temp), 7326 (precip amount + chance), 7342 (temp + humidity), 7353 (temp), 7369 (temp). Every one of those numbers is already rendered elsewhere in the same expanded card — temp and humidity in the 📡 hero at 7438–7440, dew point in the comfort line at 7453 (which also re-derives the word 'muggy' via `dewPointComfort`, so 'Muggy afternoon' and 'Dew point 68° (muggy)' both appear), today's high in the Forecast strip's Today cell, precip chance in the same cell, rain rate and today's total in the hero and twice more in the rainfall panel.
findings.user_impact: The glance sentence is the card's synthesis layer and it is currently spending its one line on data the card is about to show anyway — so the reader who came for 'so what is it doing?' gets a number, then the same number, then the same number. At half-engagement she does not read it as depth; she reads it as the app saying the same thing three ways, which is what unreliable systems do.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Lead with the synthesis, not the rows' (the synthesis is the deliverable; the rows are its evidence — a synthesis that restates the rows is not a synthesis) + 'Ordering first, then type in service of it' + 'A value's provenance and freshness must be shown as honestly as the value itself' (one value, one place, one source tag)
findings.recommendation: ONE NUMBER, ONE ALTITUDE. The glance carries MEANING; the 📡 block and the 🌐 Forecast block own the FIGURES. Exact string edits: 7286 → observation: "Rain coming down now." (rate + today are in the hero) 7293 → "Soils saturated after today's rain." 7300 → "Muggy " + partOfDay + " — heavy air, slow to dry." (temp is the hero's first value; dew point + the word 'muggy' are in the comfort line) 7316–7318 → "Hot day ahead." and delete the `tail` const (today's high is the Forecast Today cell) 7326 → "Rain likely today." and delete `amt` (amount + chance are the Forecast Today cell) 7342 → "Cool damp morning." 7353 → "Comfortable " + monthName + " " + partOfDay + ", light winds." 7310 KEEP its number — the overnight low appears nowhere else on the card, and a frost figure is the one place the number IS the meaning. 7369/7376 (the generic descriptor) → drop the temp from the sentence too, see below. ⚠️ THE ONE THING THIS BREAKS, AND ITS FIX: the collapsed header uses the same sentence (one engine, one verdict, 7/14 F1), and when the card is closed the hero is not visible — so a number-free sentence would leave the collapsed header without a temperature. Do NOT solve this by forking the generator. Solve it in `renderWeatherSummary()` (7907) only: render the sentence, then append the measured temp as its own trailing element, e.g. `72°F` (Crimson 15px/600, #1a4028, a bare 📡 oval beside it). One engine still produces the sentence; the two altitudes differ in DEPTH, which is exactly what 'the glance is a projection of the same computation, not a parallel one' prescribes. Add the matching `body.text-lg .weather-summary-temp` rule.

findings.observation: Paul asked, of line 7301's 'Fungal pressure high — water at the base, not foliage.': 'is that a plant thing, or what is that?' — and he is right that the sentence has no subject. `property.json:100` holds the actual domain knowledge for exactly this condition: high summer RH plus cloud immersion at elevation 'raises fungal pressure (boxwood blight, powdery mildew). Prioritize air circulation in plantings.' Boxwood is a real record in `PLANTS_DATA`. So the card knows what is at risk, what the risk is called, and that it grows here — and surfaces none of it.
findings.user_impact: An advisory with no subject cannot be acted on, and for a reader with difficulty it is worse than absent: it is a phrase that looks like it means something and refuses to resolve. This is also the one line on the card that could carry the property's real research depth into the glance layer, which is what 'the repository' exists for.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Meet the user at the action' (the deliverable is the next move, and a next move needs an object) + 'The glance and the repository' (the glance is a curated projection OF the repository — here the repository is right there and is not being projected) + Nielsen #2 (match between system and the real world)

findings.observation: `renderTrendStrip()` (7189) prints `.trend-now` for all three series: the current temperature, the current humidity, and the current pressure. findings.user_impact: Same class as F11, one block lower. The trend strip's job is the SHAPE of the last 24 hours; the current value is not its contribution, it is the hero's.

findings.observation: Paul's reported overflow, located: it is the day-by-day strip in the rainfall panel, and the cell that spills past the container edge is the last one — the one labelled 'Today.' `.rain-byday` is `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr)` with `gap:4px`, and `.rain-byday-cell` has no `min-width:0`, so each `1fr` track is floored at the widest cell's min-content width and the tracks CANNOT shrink. The width outlier is the label: six cells say 'Su'/'Mo' (2 chars) and one says 'Today' (5 chars), and that single long label sets the floor for all seven tracks. Arithmetic at 390px: a weather `.wblock` gives 297px of content; 7 tracks + 6×4px gaps leaves 273px, i.e. 39px per track. At base size 'Today' at 9px/0.3px-tracking needs ~30px + 4px padding + 2px border ≈ 36px — it just fits. In `body.text-lg` the label goes to 11px (line 5592) and the amount to 19px (5591), pushing the floor to ≈42px per track → 7×42 + 24 = 318px against a 297px container. The grid overflows by ~21px to the right, and since `.wblock` has no overflow rule the last cell sits over and past its own border (clipped only at `.main-card`'s `overflow:hidden`). So it breaks precisely in A+ mode on a 390px phone — Mom's configuration — and is invisible at desktop default.
findings.user_impact: A tile hanging off the edge of its box is read as breakage, not as design. This is on the rainfall panel: the exact card she reported as confusing on 7/26, the one whose repair was the app's single best trust moment. A visible layout break there spends that back.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Make every surface read at half-engagement' (the bar is the worst-case context) + the standing lesson from the 7/26 incident — on this card, anything that looks wrong is concluded to BE wrong

findings.observation: Today's rainfall is stated twice on the rainfall panel itself: `.rain-cell` labelled 'Today' in the gauge grid (renderPropertyGaugeBlock, 7156) and `.rain-byday-cell.is-today` in the day-by-day strip (7813), ~60px apart, same source, same number, two type scales (18px vs 16px) and two treatments (green fill when active vs green ring). The gauge grid's 'Now' cell and the panel header's summary line ('Raining now · 0.15"/hr') are a second such pair.
findings.user_impact: Milder than F11 but the same lesson she already taught this project: two figures on one card that look like different measurements, and are not, read as a contradiction — and the honest conclusion a reader draws from a contradiction is that the app is broken.
findings.principle_invoked: One number, one altitude (F11) + the 7/26 standing lesson: 'Two numbers on one card that measure different things must say which is which' — its converse, two numbers that measure the SAME thing must not both be there
findings.recommendation: Cut 'Today' from the gauge grid and let the by-day strip's ringed Today cell own it — the strip is the block that answers her actual ask ('look back at it day by day'), and the ring already marks today. That also takes the gauge grid from 5 cells to 4, which fits 2×2 cleanly at ≤480px and resolves the ragged 3+2 the 7/26 review flagged (F12 there). Combined with that review's still-open recommendation to cut or rename 'Event', the grid becomes Now / Last 7 Days / Month — three cells, one row, no wrap. Keep the header summary line; it is prose, not a figure.

findings.observation: Paul's question — whether an optional box should just be visible rather than sitting behind a button — has three live instances and they have never been decided by one rule: the composer's `.ui-textarea` (always visible, top of app, the ONLY surface she has reached for unprompted, 2026-07-26); `＋ Add a note` → `.mom-queue-correction` on every confirm card (disclosed; up to 5 cards can be in the queue, so always-visible would mean up to 5 open boxes in the app's scarcest vertical space); and `.feedback-panel-input`, which is always-visible once the ribbon opens the panel — i.e. the panel IS the disclosure. Telemetry cannot arbitrate directly: `card_expanded` (4 fires / 30 days / 15 sessions) measures a different control on a different surface, and the launcher's 0 taps measures a door, not a box. The one real datum is that the box she used was the always-visible one — and it is the app's only always-visible one.
findings.user_impact: Getting this wrong in either direction is expensive. Hiding the safe option behind a click on a card full of verdict buttons ranks the thing she cannot get wrong last (the 7/26 F9 finding). Opening five boxes above the dashboard strip pushes the glance she actually reads off the first screen, on zero signal, which is the star-trap in a new costume.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Defer affordances pending signal' (auto-memory) + 'Scope is communicated by where you tap, not auto-detected' + 'Friction kills — it just works' + 'The glance and the repository' (nothing may push the glance down the page without earning it)
findings.recommendation:
THE RULE, reusable: A free-response box is ALWAYS VISIBLE when all three hold — (1) writing is the surface's PRIMARY job, not a modifier on another control; (2) it is the only free-response on that screen; (3) it costs no more than about one thumb-height and does not push the glance below the fold. Otherwise it is DISCLOSED, behind a control that says in words what it opens. Tie-breaker when it is genuinely ambiguous: DISCLOSE THE SECOND BOX, NEVER THE FIRST — one screen gets at most one open box, because two open boxes force a routing decision before she has anything to say, which is the scope problem wearing a different hat.

Applied:
  • The composer — always visible. Passes all three, and it is the one open box. NO CHANGE. This is what makes every other box disclosed by rule rather than by preference.
  • `＋ Add a note` — stays DISCLOSED (fails 1 and 2, and multiplies by the queue). But two fixes it still owes, both from the 7/26 review and both verified still open in the code today: (a) the label. `addNote.textContent` at 10904 is still '＋ Add a note'. Change it to 'Tell me in your own words' — it names what opens, drops the glyph per F5, and is the register she actually uses. (b) its rank. Under F9's row grid it becomes a `.btn-choice` in the row rather than a full-bleed pill below it, so the move she cannot be wrong about sits level with the ones she can.
  • The feedback panel — correct as built; the ribbon is the disclosure and the box inside it is open. NO CHANGE.

What would change the verdict on the confirm-card box, stated in advance so it is a measurement and not an argument: if `MAX_VISIBLE` ever drops to 1, clause (2) starts passing and the box should become visible. Do not re-litigate before then.

findings.observation: Whole-viewer sweep, radii: 20 distinct values across the file, dominated by 10px (~35 uses) and 8px (~35), then 12px (~22), 9px (~17), 6px (~13), with singletons at 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 19, 20, 22, 999 and 50%. But there IS a coherent scale hiding in it, already correct at the container level: .main-card 18 → .ref-drawer-toggle 16 → .ic-card 14 → .wblock / .dash-cell 12 → .main-card-icon 11 → controls 10 → chips 8. The icon squares even hold a consistent ratio to their containers (42/11, 38/10, 28/8, ~3.8:1). The noise is almost entirely in the 5–9px range, where a dozen small elements each picked a number.
findings.user_impact: Low individually. Cumulatively it is why the app reads as slightly assembled rather than slightly designed — Paul's four-word bar is intentional · professional · clean · holistic, and a 7px radius beside a 9px radius beside a 6px radius fails the first word.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Content and function first; form follows — and then form has to be excellent' (paul-stated 2026-07-27) + Ornament earns its place
findings.recommendation: Adopt the token scale in F1 (18/16/14/12/10/8/999/50%) and do a mechanical pass: 11→12 or 10 by container level; 9, 7, 6, 5 → 8; 4, 3, 2 → keep ONLY where the element is under ~16px (a 6px dot cannot wear an 8px radius); 13→14; 19, 20, 22 on pill-shaped things → 999; 16 stays for the shelf; 18 stays for the shell. That is roughly 60 edits, all find-and-replace by value with a per-site glance, and it collapses 20 values to 8. Do it in ONE commit, separate from every behavioural change, so a regression bisects cleanly. Do not touch `.main-card` 18px or `.ic-card` 14px — they are load-bearing identity from prior waves.

findings.observation: One component, two radii: `.dash-cell` is 12px and `.dash-cell.dash-small` (Tier B) is 9px. The tier difference is already carried by background (#fff vs #fafbf5), border colour, and padding — three signals — and the 7/29 pass deliberately kept the LABEL sizes identical between tiers so they stay readable without glasses. So the radius is a fourth signal doing the same job, and the only one that makes the two tiers read as different KINDS of object rather than as two sizes of one.
findings.user_impact: Small, but it is the same failure the four input cards were standardized out of on 7/30 — 'sibling but quieter' should be one register down, not a different component.
findings.principle_invoked: 'One shell, one signal each' (proposed 2026-07-30, still unratified) + Nielsen #4
findings.recommendation: Give `.dash-cell.dash-small` the same `var(--r-block)` 12px and let background + border + padding carry the tier. If 12px reads too soft at the smaller box, take BOTH to 10px rather than splitting them.

principles_to_propose.principle: Shape is the role — a control's geometry declares what kind of act it is, and a new visual signature is a claim that a new role exists. Within one product, radius + fill + width form a CLOSED vocabulary: each shape means exactly one kind of act (commit / choose / quiet chrome / inline link), and it means it everywhere. Before styling a new control, name which role it is; if it is none of them, the burden is to argue the role exists — not to pick a radius.
principles_to_propose.target_file: ~/.claude/design-principles/cross-project/form-and-restraint.md (plus ONE line in the cross-project.md index)
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F1/F2/F4. Fernwood has 110 buttons in 31 signatures and 10 radii, and the striking thing is that a coherent system was ALREADY 90% emergent — pills were choices, rects were commits — and nobody had written it down, so every new control was a fresh decision and the rule was broken just often enough to be unlearnable. This sharpens 'Ornament earns its place' from the element level to the SYSTEM level: that rule asks whether an element earns its place; this one asks whether a new VARIANT earns its existence. It is also the mechanism behind Paul's own goal — 'conforming should be easier than inventing button #32' — which is a property of the system, not of any button. [1 occurrence — Fernwood 2026-08-02. If Paul would rather hold to the two-occurrence bar, the conservative home is cross-project/candidates.md; the likely second sighting is Bolo Boys' CTA set, where a booking CTA, an email-signup submit and an add-to-calendar pill already coexist.]

principles_to_propose.principle: A control row is even or it is stacked — never wrapped. Any row of sibling controls resolves to one of exactly two layouts: an even grid where every member is the same width and the row's outer edges land on the container's, or a full-width stack in priority order. Never `flex-wrap` on a control row: wrap produces a ragged trailing row, and empty space beside a control reads as a control that failed to load. If a member cannot fit the even row at the reader's minimum legible type size, the row stacks — it does not shrink the type.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F9. Paul's own words for the symptom — 'a row where something's missing' — are the finding: he read the gap as a missing control, which is exactly what a ragged wrap signifies whether or not anyone intended it. The trailing clause matters as much as the rule: the temptation when three buttons will not fit is to shrink the label, and on a surface with a legibility floor (Mom's 14px Crimson, the 16px input floor) that trades a visible layout flaw for an invisible accessibility one. Sits under 'Ordering first, then type in service of it' — this is the geometry half of the same idea.

principles_to_propose.principle: One number, one altitude. A value may be stated once on a surface, at the highest altitude that earns it, and every other layer refers to it rather than repeating it. A glance carries MEANING; the block that owns the source carries the FIGURE. A value restated at three altitudes in three phrasings does not read as depth — it reads as three sources that might disagree, and the reader is right to suspect that, because independently-computed restatements eventually do.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F11/F13/F15. Fernwood's weather card states the current temperature in the collapsed header, in the glance sentence, in the 📡 hero and in the trend strip; today's rainfall appears twice on one panel, sixty pixels apart, in two type scales. This belongs in honest-surfaces rather than ordering because the damage is to CREDIBILITY, not to tidiness: the reader cannot tell whether four printings are four readings, and the card's whole claim is 'measured on your property.' Companion to 'A value's provenance and freshness must be shown as honestly as the value itself' — that one says don't misrepresent where a number came from; this one says don't make one number look like several. Note the deliberate carve-out, which Paul already ratified: 'Strip teases, card holds' makes strip↔card duplication the CONTRACT, not a violation — this rule governs duplication WITHIN one surface.

principles_to_propose.principle: PROMOTE 'One engine, one verdict' from candidate to full Fernwood principle, and add the sharpening clause: two rule cascades reading the same inputs are two engines even when neither is 'the same function twice.' The tell is not duplicated code — it is two independent decision procedures over one dataset, which will have neighbouring thresholds and will eventually disagree on the same day.
principles_to_propose.target_file: ~/.claude/design-principles/fernwood.md (edit the existing candidate in place; drop the [candidate — 1 occurrence] stamp)
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F10 — the confirming second occurrence the existing entry explicitly asked for ('watch for the second occurrence in the other dual-surface concepts already latent'). 2026-07-06 caught two compute paths for one species phase and fixed it by deleting one. 2026-07-14 caught the collapsed header and the card body disagreeing and fixed it by pointing both at `generateGardenerInsight()`. Neither could see the third path, because `generateAlerts()` is not a duplicate of anything — it is a separate cascade over the same station and forecast fields, with a 0.02 rain threshold where the insight cascade uses 0.05, so on a light-rain afternoon one says it is raining and the other does not mention rain. That is the same failure as the fishing table lighting up two phases NOW, arrived at from a direction the original wording did not cover, which is why the clause is worth adding rather than just stamping a second date.

principles_to_propose.principle: One open box per screen; every other free-response is disclosed. A free-response field is always-visible only when writing is the surface's primary job, it is the only free-response on that screen, and it does not push the surface's glance below the fold. Otherwise it sits behind a control that names in WORDS what it opens. Tie-breaker: disclose the second box, never the first — two open boxes force a routing decision before the user has anything to say.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F16. Fernwood has three free-response surfaces decided three different ways, and the only behavioural signal it has (she reached for the composer unprompted, twice, on 2026-07-26) is a signal about the app's ONE always-visible box — which is an argument for keeping it singular, not for adding more. The clause about the glance is Fernwood-specific and load-bearing: the input stack sits above the dashboard strip, so any box that becomes visible spends the scarcest space in the product. Fernwood-scoped for now; the likely second sighting is Bolo Boys' email signup versus a booking-enquiry field on the same page, at which point the glance clause would need re-deriving for a page with no glance.

principles_to_propose.principle: SHARPENING CLAUSE, not a new principle — add to 'Icons earn their place — true AND useful': on a BUTTON, a glyph must carry the DECISION, never the topic. The affirmative ✓ and the negative × pass, because they encode the answer independently of whether the label can be read — which is the whole point for a reader with difficulty. A topic emoji fails, because the topic is the container's job and the label already says the act. A glyph that appears both on a card's identity square and on the button inside it has failed twice.
principles_to_propose.target_file: ~/.claude/design-principles/cross-project/form-and-restraint.md — append to the existing 'Icons earn their place' entry rather than adding a new principle
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F5. Deliberately proposed as a clause rather than a principle: the existing two-test rule already catches this, and Paul's 'Ornament earns its place' even uses the exact case as its Example ('An icon next to a Save button adds nothing — the word does the work'). What the clause adds is the ONE exception that keeps the rule from over-firing — the ✓/× on Mom's answer buttons look like decoration by the two-test rule and are in fact the most load-bearing glyphs in the app, because they carry meaning past a label she may not be able to read. Naming the exception is what makes the rule safe to apply without asking each time.
